The data shows NT-proBNP geometric mean at 9 months was 2332.1 ng/L in the guided arm vs. 2063 ng/L in the not-guided arm — paradoxically, the guided arm had HIGHER NT-proBNP levels, suggesting the biomarker-guided strategy did not achieve superior neurohormonal suppression compared to clinical guidance alone. This is a critical finding: the strategy intended to optimize therapy to lower NT-proBNP did not result in lower NT-proBNP levels. 2. The titration steps were similar (517 guided vs. 485 not-guided), suggesting the NT-proBNP guidance did not meaningfully change the intensity of therapy. The underlying neurohormonal blockade biology was presumably engaged in both arms similarly, as both received guideline-directed medical therapy. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: The primary composite endpoint (rank score of CV death, CV hospitalization days, KCCQ symptoms at 9 months) was not met. The guided arm had a mean rank score of 118.6 vs. 128.4 in the not-guided arm (lower score = worse outcome), meaning the guided arm actually trended numerically worse, though no p-value was reported suggesting the difference was not statistically significant. The clinical endpoint did not improve with NT-proBNP guidance. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup findings were reported. The enrolled population was heart failure patients with LV dysfunction and elevated NT-proBNP (functional class II, low LVEF, high NT-proBNP) — a reasonable population for this strategy. 5. CONFOUNDERS: The trial was relatively small (N=252) and may have been underpowered to detect a modest difference in the composite endpoint. The 9-month duration may have been insufficient. Importantly, the control arm also received active guideline-directed therapy, creating a high-quality comparator that may have compressed the detectable treatment effect. The failure appears primarily to reflect that NT-proBNP-guided titration did not produce meaningfully different therapy intensification compared to clinical guidance alone in this population and timeframe — the strategy failed to differentiate the two arms in terms of actual treatment delivered or NT-proBNP achieved.
